text:
alice: Heads-up — customer ACME reported a sudden p99 jump on /v1/generate from ~80ms to ~1.2s starting 12:21UTC. They say requests are being routed to eu-central while they’re in us-west. Anyone else seeing geo detours? :eyes:

ben: seeing alerts too, p95->p99 drift on host pool us-west-1. No deploys in the last hour from eng-runtime. Can you paste a trace?

cara: I’ve got a sample trace from the customer (redacted ids). Trace shows request enters edge-us-west then next hop is 34.239.###.### (eu egress) which is wrong. They included a traceroute: 

cara: ```
traceroute to api.redwood.ai (34.239.xxx.xxx), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  edge-usw-01 (10.0.0.2)  0.4 ms  0.3 ms  0.4 ms
 2  core-router-usw (10.1.0.1)  1.2 ms  1.1 ms  1.1 ms
 3  backbone-1 (52.95.xxx.xxx)  5.8 ms  5.7 ms  5.6 ms
 4  34.239.xxx.xxx (34.239.xxx.xxx)  1100 ms  1200 ms  1188 ms
```

cara: that 34.239.* looks like an eu NAT we don't expect for this customer.

devops-bot: route-policy-change detected by config-watcher at 2026-03-10T12:20:58Z: fallback-policy=v2-global-edge enabled for pool us-west-1 by laura.rolling (intent: resilience during partial failure).

ben: ah — fallback-policy flip at ~12:20 aligns perfectly. Is v2-global-edge egressing from eu for some prefixes?

laura: I rolled the fallback to v2-global-edge as a temporary mitigation for a separate internal imbalance. That pool has a subset of edge nodes in eu-central that act as global failover. I messed up the prefix match; it’s defaulting more broadly than intended. Sorry.

alice: ok that explains hop. But why was the customer routed there at all (not just during auth failures)? We saw both high-latency successes and a spike in 401s around the same time.

laura: investigating logs — looks like our auth-svc in edge-us-west returned transient 401 on first token validation for ~30s due to a short memcache blip. The router has a policy: on auth failure try fallback pool. So chains: auth 401 -> router sends to fallback -> fallback egress in eu -> latency spike.

ben: reproduce steps (quick):
1) curl -v -H "Host: api.redwood.ai" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://edge-usw.example.redwood/v1/generate
2) if you force an auth fail (e.g., bad token), router should hit fallback.

cara: customer ran a tcpdump, sample (redacted):
```
12:21:05.123 IP client -> edge-usw: SYN
12:21:05.124 IP edge-usw -> auth-svc: request validate
12:21:05.154 IP auth-svc -> edge-usw: 401
12:21:05.156 IP edge-usw -> 34.239.xxx.xxx: forward to fallback pool
```

alice: plan: revert fallback-policy to previous narrower match, patch router to not escalate to cross-region egress on transient auth 401s, and notify ACME. Laura can you rollback the fallback rule?

laura: I've scoped the policy to only target prefix 10.2.0.0/16 (internal experimental) and redeployed at 12:28UTC. Monitoring now.

devops-bot: rollout complete: policy-scope-update by laura at 2026-03-10T12:28:10Z (canary 3/3, no errors).

ben: after rollback p99 for ACME dropped back to ~95ms within two minutes. No further eu hops in new traces.

cara: advised customer to keep an eye on any residual 401s and asked for logs between 12:15-12:40UTC. They appreciated the quick turnaround. :+1:

alice: follow-ups:
- laura to open PR to change router behavior for auth-failures (dont fallback cross-region on single 401).
- eng-runtime to add alert for 'fallback-routed-to-foreign-egress' metric.
- support to update runbook with tcpdump/traceroute checklist.

laura: starting PR now. will tag ben for review.

ben: thanks everyone, good triage. Marking thread resolved for now — will reopen if ACME sees anything else.

cara: adding final note to ticket: root cause = mis-scoped fallback-policy + transient auth memcache blip -> cross-region fallback egress -> p99 spike.

alice: :white_check_mark:
